title: An Optimal Diffusion Approach to Quadratic Rate-Distortion Problems: New Solution and Approximation Methods
claim: As the trade-off parameter grows, a smooth distribution gradually collapses into a singular one, tracing a continuum between two extremes.
layout: 1 panel, 3D axes, family of curves evolving along an arrow
description: A single 3D-style schematic in a light gray box. A family of green curves represents the reconstruction density at different values of the parameter epsilon. The curves are spaced along a depth axis. On the right, the curves are pale and smooth. Moving left, they get darker and more jagged, and they end in a thick, near-vertical green line that stands for a singular distribution. A thick blue curve at the top right marks the low-distortion end, where the reconstruction is close to the source. Bold black labels 'Low-distortion' and 'Low-rate' mark the two ends. A dark teal arrow below the box points left and is labeled epsilon. A rotated green 'rec. density' label sits on the left. The eye goes first to the dark green spike and the blue curve.
caption: Evolution of reconstruction distributions w.r.t. parameter ϵ. Typically, we assume the reconstruction density to be close to the continuous source in the low distortion regime (small ϵ’s), while eventually becoming singular for a low enough rate (large ϵ’s).
abstract: When compressing continuous data, some loss of information is inevitable, and this incurred a distortion upon reconstruction. The Rate–Distortion (RD) function characterizes the minimum achievable rate for a code whose decoding permits a specified amount of distortion. We exploit the connection between rate-distortion theory and entropic optimal transport to propose a novel stochastic-control formulation for the former, and use a classic result dating back to Schrodinger to show that the tradeoff between rate and mean squared error distortion is equivalent to a tradeoff between control energy and the differential entropy of the terminal state, whose probability law defines the reconstruction distribution. For a special class of sources, we show that the optimal control law and the corresponding trajectory in the space of probability measures are obtained by solving a backward heat equation. In more general settings, our approach yields a numerical method that estimates the RD function using diffusion processes with a constant diffusion coefficient. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through several examples.
